twfe_decomposition_theorem_3_4a.note: weights computed on the 2024 dose over all 49 units; exact for the 2024 cross-section, indicative for the year-averaged linear series

comparison_table.identifying_assumption: Strict exogeneity of capacity conditional on state and year FE; no time-varying state shock correlated with both capacity and employment.
comparison_table.likely_bias_direction: Attenuated by classical measurement error in the capacity series; sign ambiguous under reverse causality (firms site where the tech labour force already grows) -- that channel biases UP.
comparison_table.note: panel_fe_table__contig49.csv, 49 units, N = 438, finite-sample-corrected clustered SE with t(48) inference

comparison_table.identifying_assumption: Parallel trends between states that cross 1 GW and states that never do, plus no anticipation. Control group is NOT untreated.
comparison_table.likely_bias_direction: Attenuated toward zero: the control group contains states that added up to 1 GW, so the contrast understates the true level effect. Offsetting upward bias if crossing 1 GW is itself selected on booming tech employment.
comparison_table.note: published ATT = 3,813 jobs (SE 1,175), 13 treated / 36 control, N = 438, read from 06_staggered_did_analysis.xlsx; divided by a dose contrast of 2.1930 GW

comparison_table.identifying_assumption: As above at the 500 MW threshold.
comparison_table.likely_bias_direction: Same direction; worse, because the control group is even more contaminated at the lower threshold.
comparison_table.note: published ATT = 1,526 jobs (SE 1,423), 18 treated / 31 control, N = 438, read from 06_staggered_did_analysis.xlsx; dose contrast 1.8093 GW

comparison_table.identifying_assumption: STRONG parallel trends (paper, Assumption SPT): E[Y_2(d)-Y_1(0)|D>0] = E[Y_2(d)-Y_1(0)|D=d] for all d, i.e. the group that took dose d is a valid counterfactual for the whole treated population at that dose. NOT nested with binary parallel trends -- it does not require parallel trends in untreated potential outcomes for all dose groups -- but in an application like this one it is a much stronger assumption, and it is untestable because it restricts counterfactual TREATED outcomes. The parameter identified is ACRT^glob (Corollary 3.1(b)), not ACRT^loc.
comparison_table.likely_bias_direction: Biased by selection on gains if states with the largest build-outs would have had the steepest tech-employment growth anyway -- that is an UPWARD bias. Downward bias from measurement error in the dose.
comparison_table.note: quadratic series, averaged over 2017-2024, bootstrap SE over states

comparison_table.method: Continuous DiD, ACRT^o at d = 1 GW
comparison_table.identifying_assumption: STRONG parallel trends (Assumption SPT), evaluated at a fixed policy-relevant dose rather than averaged over the realised dose distribution. The parameter is ACRT(d) (Theorem 3.3(c)).
comparison_table.likely_bias_direction: Same as the ACRT. Reported separately because the estimated dose-response is concave, so the average over realised doses (dominated by many small-dose states) exceeds the response at 1 GW.

comparison_table.identifying_assumption: STRONG parallel trends; states weighted by the capacity they added, so this is the response relevant to the national job total.
comparison_table.likely_bias_direction: Pulled down relative to the ACRT by the concavity of the dose-response: the marginal GW in TX/VA/OR adds fewer jobs than the first GW anywhere.
comparison_table.note: quadratic series, E[D*ACRT(D)]/E[D] over treated states

comparison_table.identifying_assumption: Exogeneity of the 2019 exposure shares conditional on state and year FE (Goldsmith-Pinkham/Borusyak share exogeneity), UNION leave-out national shift (state + contiguous + division), 49 units.
comparison_table.likely_bias_direction: Above the FE estimate as classical attenuation and a compliers-weighted LATE both predict. Residual risk: share endogeneity if 2019 capacity shares proxy a persistent state trend.
comparison_table.note: 05_bartik_iv.py, union leave-out, 49 units, N = 291, Olea-Pflueger effective F = 29.8
